label: prf:nuclear-knot-classification
title: Proof of nuclear knot classification
html:
Proof. The nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z,N) is built by interleaving Z proton NFs and N neutron NFs with typed crossings (pp, nn, pn). Each nucleon NF is the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 dressed with quark crossings.

For A = 3: the three nucleon NFs compose to give a braid whose NF has alternating \sigma_0, \sigma_1 signs and dominant L_+ (Hopf link) content. This is the NF signature of the figure-eight knot 4_1 = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1, verified by comparing eigenvalue structure.

For A \geq 4: the composition of four or more nucleon NFs produces identity-dominated NF with small Hopf corrections — the signature of the Borromean link, confirmed by the Frobenius positivity G \cdot x \geq 0 at all six basis channels.

The binding scale follows from the topological mass formula (topological mass formula): \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2. The volume determines the energy scale at which the nuclear braid binds.

The figure-eight volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.030 is the SAME volume that defines the substrate parameter q_0 through \hbar_q^2 = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/(m_\mu/m_e). So A = 3 nuclei bind at the scale set by the substrate itself. \square
